html:
The Dieri, or Diyari, are an Aboriginal Australian people of the South Australian desert, in and around the delta of Cooper Creek east of Lake Eyre. The map shows them from 1600 to 1800.

Their country is a land of sandhills, gibber plains and channels that flood only after big rains far to the north. People relied on deep knowledge of waterholes and on seeds such as nardoo, ground into flour. Trade routes ran through their land, carrying pituri, a native tobacco, and red ochre over long distances.

In the 1860s Lutheran missionaries from Germany set up a mission at Lake Killalpaninna in Dieri country. They learned the language and wrote it down, so Dieri became one of the better recorded languages of inland Australia. Neighbours on the map include the Yandruwandha, the Ngamini and the Pirlatapa. See Aboriginal Australian societies.
